verdict.rationale: Daytona documents its own sandbox isolation: each sandbox gets a dedicated kernel, filesystem and network stack, and a firewall that blocks untrusted code from exfiltrating data. That implies host files and credentials are out of reach of agent-run code. The docs never say outright that host secrets or credentials are unreachable, so the story's core promise is inferred rather than documented. Missing for 10: explicit documentation that host secrets and credentials are inaccessible from the sandbox, a credential or secret-handling model (e.g. scoped injection without exposure), and independent or hands-on verification of the isolation boundary.

support.subject: As an ai-native user, I can give an agent a sandbox where host secrets and credentials are unreachable by the code it runs

citations.quote: Each sandbox runs in isolation, giving it a dedicated kernel, filesystem, network stack, and allocated vCPU, RAM, and disk.
Each sandbox runs behind a firewall that restricts which external IP addresses and domains it can reach, preventing untrusted code from exfiltrating data or contacting arbitrary hosts.
Daytona also provides VM sandboxes with a dedicated Linux VM or Windows operating system
